note: Primitive camping on the mown grass beside the gravel boat-ramp lot at the north-west end of a 19-acre lake in the woods; the water is 10-25 m away with nothing between. No pads, tables or toilet, and the lot is shared with anglers launching. --Claude
summary: Stays under the lot rule: MDC marks a Primitive Camping Area (map symbol + GIS point) on the grass at the edge of the ramp lot. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; phone matches; pin on the point. Lakefront stands (open grass to the water, 10-25 m), with the caveat that the one spot is the ramp lot's own apron.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays, as Lick Creek): page: 'forested tract contains a 19 acre lake with boat ramp and offers hunting, fishing and camping'; 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'. No brochure. The map (04/08) legend has Primitive Camping Area and draws the symbol right beside the Parking Lot and Boat Ramp at the lake's north-west end. GIS layer 27: one point at 40.26198,-93.07544 = stored pin; the lot is 24 m west. On imagery: a gravel lot about 45 x 20 m running down to the ramp, mown grass about 25 m deep on its east and south sides, and the GIS point on that grass. No pads or loop. 83 acres.

WATERFRONT (stored lakefront stands): from the GIS point the water is about 20 m south and 25 m east across mown grass with no trees; from the lot's lower end under 10 m. Open apron, well inside 50 m. The only thing sharing it is the ramp, which is day use on the same lot - there is no separate camp behind it, so I have left lakefront; drop to lakeview if a ramp lot's apron should not count.
DIRECTIONS: the stored note said Route RA north 2.5 miles (from the page); the map labels the access road Finch Drive. Directions taken out of the note.
PIN: on the GIS point. No move.
